text:
Maya: dropped a compact p95-row prototype in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/yyyyyy (frame: compact-p95-rows). want quick feedback on four things: how/where to show sample size (n=), bucket strategy (fixed vs adaptive), keyboard nav for tiny rows, and whether "p95" label needs more clarity.

Alex: skimmed it. love the n= pill idea. main concern: top-right placement gets clipped when the panel is narrow. maybe put n= inside the metric chip itself so it collapses together. also small widths need truncation rules. :mag_right:

Ravi: about buckets 12: adaptive binning looks visually tidy but bucket boundaries shift when users pan/zoom. that makes cross-row comparisons hard. i'd vote fixed bucket breakpoints (e.g., 0-10,10-50,50-200,200+) with an optional percentiles overlay line so you can still see p50/p95 trends.

Noor: accessibility notes: please provide a colorblind-safe palette + pattern overlay toggle for users who prefer textures. also ensure screen readers can get sample size and whether the data is sampled or exact via aria-describedby. example: "p95: 320 ms (n=27, sampled)".

Taylor: keyboard nav is broken in the compact rows right now because every cell is a plain div. we should make cells focusable (role=button, tabindex=0) and support arrow keys to move left/right. on focus announce via aria-live: "bucket 3 of 6, 0.8% requests, p95 420 ms". tiny suggestion: keep focus ring thin so it doesn't obscure neighbors.

Maya: good call. what about motion when changing sampling granularity? currently we morph bar heights which is jarring. propose crossfade between old/new data for >200ms transitions, and immediate update for faster interactions.

Alex: copy nit: users outside infra sometimes don't get "p95" label. suggest expanding to "95th percentile latency (ms)" with a hover tooltip: "The value that 95% of requests are faster than." keep short label "p95" as small de-emphasized token.

Ravi: small-sample UX: if n < 20 show a low-sample warning inline: "Low sample 12 p95 may be unstable" and dim the percentile overlay but keep numeric visible. also show the sampling rate (rows/sec) in the settings flyout.

DesignerBot: accessibility check: recommended palette for compact rows (colorblind-safe) and a low-contrast pattern. tokens:
```
--heat-1: #ffffff; /* background */
--heat-2: #edf2f7; /* light */
--heat-3: #cbd5e1; /* mid */
--heat-4: #2b8a3e; /* high (colorblind-safe) */
--pattern: url('/assets/diag-2.svg');
--focus-ring: 2px solid #0ea5e9;
```
Contrast note: if we overlay text on top of heat cells we must keep >=4.5:1. for non-textual marks (cells) a lower ratio is acceptable but provide pattern alternative.

Maya: plan of attack:
1) move n= into metric chip and add truncation rules for tiny widths
2) switch to fixed bucket breakpoints by default, enable adaptive as opt-in in settings
3) make cells focusable (role/button) + arrow-key nav + aria-live announcements
4) change label to "95th percentile latency (ms)" with short tooltip and de-emphasized "p95" token
5) show low-sample badge when n < 20 and dim percentile overlay
6) crossfade data on granularity changes >200ms, immediate otherwise

Noor: sounds great. please also add an a11y toggle in the dashboard settings to force patterns on for all users.

Taylor: dev note: here's a tiny CSS snippet for focus + n-pill collapse rules:
```
.cell[role=button]:focus { outline: var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 1px; }
.metric-chip .n-pill { margin-left: 8px; white-space: nowrap; }
@media (max-width: 420px) { .metric-chip .n-pill { display: none; } }
```

Maya: thanks everyone 12 i'll update the figma with fixed buckets, n-pill inside chip, aria attributes, and the low-sample state. i'll post the new frame when done and tag everyone. :thumbsup:
